name: Singular Anaphoric they
pattern: anaphoric NP[they/them/their] with a singular referent or antecedent

entry.name: Singular Anaphoric they
entry.pattern: anaphoric NP[they/them/their] with a singular referent or antecedent

1.definition: Uses the they paradigm for a single antecedent, including a bound variable or a known person.

projection.target: The antecedent can be singular while they takes ordinary they-agreement, such as were. The construction is compatible with bound readings and with specific references in suitable contexts.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: They for one person
curious.summary: They, them and their can point back to a single person, and the verb still agrees as it does with they.
curious.body: In Every applicant said they were ready, the word they refers back to every applicant, taken one at a time. The verb is were, the same form used when they means several people. The pattern is also compatible with they for a specific person in a suitable context. The word that they refers back to is singular, while the pronoun still takes its usual they forms. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional.
curious.try: Say a sentence beginning Everyone said ... and finish it with they. Which verb form follows?

teacher.summary: Helps explain they, them and their with a singular antecedent.
teacher.explain: The they paradigm (they, them, their) can have a singular antecedent, including a bound-variable reading (as with every applicant) or a known person. In Every applicant said they were ready, the antecedent is singular, yet they takes ordinary they-agreement, such as were. The pattern is compatible with bound readings and with specific references in suitable contexts. This dictionary treats it as a specialization of the personal pronoun NP and relates it to verb number agreement. The analysis is marked provisional.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called singular they. In this dictionary: singular anaphoric they.
watch_for: A learner might expect the verb to agree with the singular antecedent (every applicant), when they takes ordinary they-agreement, such as were.
A learner might assume they can only refer to more than one person.
teacher.activity: Students complete sentences starting Each student said ... and Every player thought ... using they, then circle the verb and discuss its form.

child.hook: Can they ever mean just one person?
child.explain: Sometimes they points back to one person at a time. Every applicant said they were ready. The verb is were, just like when they means a group.
child.play: Start a sentence with Every kid said or Each player said. Finish it using they and a verb.

checked.note: Fixed: teacher explanation no longer calls every applicant the 'bound variable' (it is the antecedent; they gets the bound-variable reading); reworded an unflagged watch_for item that implied was is wrong, which the entry does not state.
